_aliases.azure/gpt-5.6-sol: GPT-5.6 Sol through the litellm proxy's Azure deployment. $4.00 input / $0.40 cached / $20.00 output per million (developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol, read 2026-09-02). THESE ARE PROMOTIONAL RATES, stated as running at least through 2026-11-21; the standard rates are $5.00/$30.00 and a sweep priced after that date under this table version will understate spend. The >272k-token tier (2x input, 1.5x output) is not used: convlog prompts are capped near 5k tokens.
_aliases.openai/Azure/gpt-4.1: same model as openai/gpt-4.1, reached through the litellm proxy under its Azure deployment id; rate copied rather than re-sourced so the two cannot drift. ADDING A KEY RE-PRICES NOTHING: every run that resolved this pin before the row existed raised LLMConfigError, recorded $0.00 and counted the message in user_sim_unpriced_msgs, so no finished figure moves and the counter is what makes the gap auditable. Measured on the lane L4.1 costing: 98 of 98 user-simulator messages unpriced.

_aliases.openai/aws/claude-opus-5: Claude Opus 5 reached through the litellm proxy's AWS deployment; the key is the full string passed to --model, because that is what the pricing lookup sees. List price $5/$25 per million (anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5, read 2026-09-02). cached_input is the published 'up to 90% savings with prompt caching' applied to the input rate.
_aliases.openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5: Claude Sonnet 5 through the litellm proxy's AWS deployment. $2/$10 per million, stated as permanent rather than introductory (anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-5, read 2026-09-03). cached_input is the published 'up to 90% savings with prompt caching' applied to input.
_aliases.openai/gcp/gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview through the litellm proxy's GCP deployment. Standard tier, prompts <= 200k tokens: $2.00/$12.00 per million (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, read 2026-09-02); the >200k tier is $4/$18 and is NOT used here -- the convlog prompts are capped near 5k tokens. cached_input is set EQUAL to input because the source publishes no cached rate for this model: assuming a discount would understate spend, and a null reads as zero in `usd`, which is the same mistake in a worse disguise.

_cached_semantics: tok_cached is a SUBSET of tok_prompt. The uncached remainder is billed at input, the cached part at cached_input. A provider that reports cached tokens disjointly would be double-counted, so adapters must normalise to the subset convention.
_why: USD is computed as tokens x these rates and NEVER read from a provider response field. A provider's dollar figure depends on account tier, promotional credits and the day it was billed, so it is not reproducible from an artifact; this table is. Rates are list prices as published 2026-08 and are pinned by ModelPin.price_table_version, so re-pricing a finished sweep is a re-read of parquet rather than a re-run.
_why_2026_09: Adds azure/gpt-5.6-terra, the deployment PI_MODEL_ANNOTATOR is pinned to. A NEW VERSION rather than an edit to 2026-08, because ModelPin.price_table_version records which table a run was priced under and editing 2026-08 in place would silently re-price every finished sweep citing it. Rates read from OpenAI's own model documentation (developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra) on 2026-08-31: input $2, cached input $0.2, output $12 per 1M tokens. Sol and Luna are deliberately ABSENT: their input and output rates are public ($5/$30 and $0.20/$1.20) but their CACHED-input rates were not on the page read, and a guessed rate in this table is the silent-zero failure it exists to prevent. Add them when someone has read the number.
_why_local_deployments: The qwen3-8b-* and qwen3-4b-* rows are LOCALLY SERVED weights: the vLLM process on the rented box (plan I.14) publishes one --lora-modules name per checkpoint, and nobody bills per token for them. $0.0 is the only honest per-token rate. Their real cost is GPU-HOUR AMORTISATION of the rented box, which a per-token table cannot express and which is recorded in the compute section of the plan instead; reading a $0 here as 'this arm was free' is a misreading of the table, not of the arm. The rows exist because PriceTable.rates is strict -- an unpriced model raises LLMConfigError -- so without them a sweep against the box refuses to start. WHY THIS IS AN EDIT TO 2026-09 AND NOT A NEW VERSION: _why_2026_09 forbids editing a table a finished sweep was priced under, because ModelPin.price_table_version records which table priced a run. That prohibition is on CHANGING A RATE. These ids have never run -- measured 2026-09-11, `calls.parquet WHERE model LIKE '%qwen%'` returns 0 rows -- so naming them re-prices nothing that exists.
